
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| label: tbl-module-content
#| tbl-cap: "Detailed description of the WBI content."

library(here)
library(gt)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

library(gt)

# Korrigierte Daten (ohne `-` am Anfang der Zeilen, nur Zeilenumbrüche)
Intervention <- c(
  "- Participants develop intrinsic motivation by identifying personal values and future aspirations, enhancing treatment readiness and reducing resistance to change.\n\n- They learn to recognize cognitive distortions and impulsivity, improving decision-making by weighing long-term consequences over immediate rewards.\n\n- Through structured goal-setting techniques, participants transform abstract desires into specific, measurable, and achievable objectives, increasing self-efficacy and behavioral clarity.\n\n- The module integrates goal implementation into reoffending prevention, reinforcing consistent behavior, coping strategies, and supervision awareness to support sustained rehabilitation.",
  
  "- Participants develop skills to build trust and collaborative working relationships with probation officers, reducing resistance and improving adherence to supervision mandates.\n\n- They identify trauma- and fear-based avoidance patterns that interfere with engagement, using cognitive-behavioral strategies to enhance compliance with structured interventions.\n\n- Through guided reflection, participants examine the impact of adult relationships on emotional regulation and behavioral stability, targeting deficits in capacity for adult intimacy.\n\n- They learn evidence-based techniques to recognize and disengage from negative social influences while cultivating prosocial, emotionally supportive relationships to sustain long-term reintegration.",
  
  "- Participants learn to identify emotions as indicators of unmet needs, reducing impulsive reactions by linking affective states to underlying psychological demands.\n\n- Through mindfulness exercises and case examples, they develop non-reactive awareness of emotions and bodily sensations, improving impulse control and reducing maladaptive coping.\n\n- They distinguish between emotional experiences and action urges using tools like the tension scale, fostering pause-and-reflect strategies to interrupt impulsive behaviors.\n\n- By creating personalized skill sets, participants build adaptive, individualized responses to emotional distress, enhancing long-term emotional regulation and self-management.",
  
  "- Participants learn to recognize problem-solving deficits as a core component of self-regulation difficulties, understanding that challenges are manageable through structured, cognitive-behavioral approaches.\n\n- They are taught the 7-Step Problem-Solving Plan to systematically identify, define, and address problems, enhancing decision-making and reducing impulsive or avoidant reactions.\n\n- Through video examples and case studies, participants practice distinguishing between changeable and unchangeable issues, generating realistic solutions, and evaluating outcomes.\n\n- The module fosters cognitive restructuring and emotional regulation by linking problem-solving to adaptive coping, promoting long-term self-regulation and behavioral control.",
  
  "- Participants learn to identify three out of 16 offense-supportive cognitive distortions, such as rationalizations that minimize harm, which perpetuate antisocial thinking and increase reoffending risk.\n\n- They explore how these distortions arise from selective attention to partial truths, reinforcing denial and minimizing consequences through psychological defense mechanisms.\n\n- Through psychoeducation and cognitive restructuring, participants challenge distorted beliefs using evidence-based techniques, promoting critical evaluation of harmful thought patterns.\n\n- Case studies and video examples illustrate real-world consequences of distorted thinking, bridging the gap between perceived justification and actual harm, enhancing insight and accountability.",
  
  "- Participants learn to differentiate between healthy and problematic sexual interests, recognizing how sexual preoccupation increases reoffending risk and undermines abstinence.\n\n- The module addresses emotional congruence with children as a key risk factor, emphasizing the importance of maintaining emotional and physical boundaries to reduce relapse potential.\n\n- Cognitive restructuring techniques are used to challenge distorted beliefs about sexual behavior, fostering insight and promoting adaptive, non-harmful thought patterns.\n\n- Through identification of high-risk triggers and personalized coping strategies, participants enhance self-regulation, self-efficacy, and control over problematic sexual urges."
)

Placebo <- c(
  "- Participants gain insight into the benefits of physical activity, identify personal barriers, and set achievable goals to build motivation for physical activity.\n\n- They develop foundational motor skills, coordination, and balance, enhancing physical confidence and improving participation in daily and therapeutic activities.\n\n- Through mindfulness and adaptive exercises, participants strengthen cognitive and emotional flexibility, reducing rigidity and improving resilience to stress.\n\n- Practical strategies are introduced to break sedentary patterns, increasing awareness of health risks and promoting sustainable, active living for long-term well-being.",
  
  "- Participants learn the basics of muscle structure and function, increasing self-awareness of physical capabilities and enhancing motivation to engage in structured physical routines.\n\n- Using the Rubicon model, they explore intrinsic and extrinsic motivators, identifying barriers like low confidence or time constraints that affect adherence and relationship-building.\n\n- By reflecting on personal sport preferences, participants recognize how peer or cultural influences may shape physical activity choices, reducing susceptibility to negative social pressures.\n\n- They gain accurate knowledge of exercise’s physiological benefits, including mood-enhancing effects and age-related misconceptions, fostering long-term commitment to healthy habits.",
  
  "- Participants learn how sleep quality directly influences emotional regulation, cognitive function, and physical health, addressing impulsivity and emotional dysregulation that undermine sleep hygiene.\n\n- Understanding sleep cycles and physiological restoration helps link poor sleep to heightened stress, supporting those with external or sexualized coping patterns in developing healthier responses.\n\n- Practical, non-drug strategies are taught to manage shift work and jetlag, promoting consistent routines and environmental adjustments that support long-term sleep stability.\n\n- Discussion of sleep disorders like apnea emphasizes their impact on health and relationships, encouraging proactive, evidence-based lifestyle changes over medication reliance.",
  
  "- Participants explore the neuroscience of dreaming, including REM and non-REM sleep stages, to understand how disrupted sleep impairs cognitive flexibility.\n\n- Through mindfulness, dream journaling, and symbolic interpretation, they develop reflective practices that enhance self-awareness.\n\n- The module links stress, sleep disruption, and dream content, illustrating how chronic stress undermines executive function and exacerbates difficulties in structured thinking and solution generation.\n\n- Case studies highlight trauma-related dream patterns, showing how unresolved psychological distress and poor sleep hinder insight and cognitive restoration, reinforcing the need for integrated sleep and emotional care.",
  
  "- Participants gain foundational knowledge of nutrition, digestion, and the mind-body connection, challenging offense-supportive beliefs by linking healthy eating to self-control and well-being.\n\n- Through case studies and interactive exercises, they explore ethical, health, and environmental motivations for plant-based diets, fostering empathy and prosocial decision-making.\n\n- Awareness of key nutrients and deficiency risks promotes informed choices, countering misinformation and supporting mental clarity and emotional stability.\n\n- Practical skills in meal planning and grocery shopping build confidence and sustainability, empowering lasting dietary changes that enhance psychological health and reduce behavioral risk.",
  
  "- Well-being is understood as a holistic, individualized experience integrating physical, psychological, and social health, rooted in emotional fulfillment, resilience, and meaningful connections.\n\n- Participants challenge the myth of universal well-being, recognizing its subjective nature and the importance of personal values, identity, and life context in shaping health and satisfaction.\n\n- Through interactive learning, participants explore the gut-brain axis, mindful eating, and hygiene practices, linking nutrition, self-care, and bodily awareness to mental clarity and psychological stability.\n\n- Psychological well-being is distinguished from happiness, focusing on meaning, inner balance, and personal growth, explored through reflections on identity, nature, music, and laughter."
)

Module <- c("Module 1", "Module 2", "Module 3", "Module 4", "Module 5", "Module 6")

# Erstelle die Tabelle
tbl_dat <- data.frame(Module, Intervention, Placebo)

# Erstelle die gt-Tabelle mit korrekter Formatierung
tbl <- gt(tbl_dat) %>%
  gt::cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = everything()
  ) %>%
  gt::fmt_markdown(
    columns = everything(),
    rows = everything()
  ) %>%
  gt::tab_options(
      #table.font.names = "Source Sans Pro",
      table.font.size = 12,
      quarto.use_bootstrap = FALSE,
      data_row.padding = px(2),
      summary_row.padding = gt::px(2),
      grand_summary_row.padding = gt::px(2),
      #footnotes.padding = gt::px(2),
      #source_notes.padding = gt::px(2),
      row_group.padding = gt::px(2)
    )

# save tbl as image
gt::gtsave(tbl, file = file.path(here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.pdf")))
#gt::gtsave(tbl, file = file.path(here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.docx")))
gt::gtsave(tbl, file = file.path(here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.png")))

tbl 

library(flextable)
library(officer)

ft <- flextable(tbl_dat) |>
  align(align = "left", part = "all") |>
  fontsize(size = 12, part = "all") |>
  padding(
    padding.top = 2,
    padding.bottom = 2,
    padding.left = 4,
    padding.right = 4,
    part = "all"
  ) |>
  autofit()

doc <- read_docx()
doc <- body_add_flextable(doc, ft)

print(
  doc,
  target = here::here("_tables/tbl-module-content.docx")
)
```
